solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flog reduced plonk to turn over wines

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter of the synonym for flog is dropped

parts.note: to flog is to whip

indicators.note: turning over a word means reading its letters backwards

parts.note: to plonk something down is to set it

explanation.surface: Someone sells off cheap wine at a cut price, flipping it for better bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts WHIP to WHI; 'to turn over' reverses SET to TES. 'Plonk' looks like cheap wine but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Whites is the usual plural for white wines, as ordered by the glass or bottle.

clue.text: House fires, fast ones

parts.note: to fire someone is to axe them, so fires gives axes

explanation.surface: A list of house fires, apparently quick ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fires' looks like flames but is the verb meaning sacks.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull a fast one is to play a trick, and a hoax is exactly such a deception.

clue.text: Entertainer can depart after performing

indicators.note: performing letters are made to act out a new arrangement, so the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer is free to leave once the show is done.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer who performs in metal-tipped shoes is one kind of stage entertainer.

clue.text: Policeman put on cases in general unwelcome binder

parts.note: a super is a superintendent, a senior police officer

indicators.note: the cases of a word are its outside letters, here taken from each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A senior officer arrives and generally brings an unwelcome folder.
explanation.walkthrough: A super is a superintendent in British police ranks; 'binder' suggests a folder but means a glue.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong adhesive binds things together, so it can be called a binder.

clue.text: Protective stuff, indefinite amount for India

indicators.note: one letter stands for another, so the I of the synonym is swapped out

parts.note: stuff, as in fabric or substance, is material
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet
n is the mathematical symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: A shopper wants protective fabric but in an unspecified quantity for India.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother's instincts are typically protective, so motherly behaviour can be described this way.

clue.text: Small bottles are historically for alcohol

indicators.note: to bottle up is to hold inside, so the synonym for small encloses the other piece

parts.note: mini means small
art is the old form of are, as in 'thou art'

explanation.surface: In the past small bottles were used for spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning holds in; 'historically' flags the archaic 'thou art'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin-and-vermouth cocktail is a drink containing alcohol, here named loosely by its contents.

clue.text: Narrow stick originally rod

parts.note: to stick something down is to tape it

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the next word, its first letter

explanation.surface: A thin stick was at first just a rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Narrow' is a verb here, not an adjective describing the stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To taper is to become gradually thinner towards one end, i.e. to narrow.

clue.text: Perch caught up in net, so organised

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
caught means held inside, so the letters lie within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A fish is caught in a net, so it's all arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perch' tempts as the fish caught in the net, but it is the bird's resting place; 'organised' is not an anagram signal here, it just supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a place where birds settle to rest, i.e. a perch.

clue.text: Lust of rapper — it's cited to be completely endless

indicators.note: completely endless means each of the three words loses both its ends

explanation.surface: A rap star's desire is quoted as boundless.
explanation.walkthrough: Stripping the ends gives APPE, T and ITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite and lust both name a strong desire or craving, e.g. a lust for life.

clue.text: Graduate doctor, one for each player

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts
a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
I is the Roman numeral for one
per means for each, as in 'per person'

explanation.surface: A graduate doctor allocates one to each person playing.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician on the bagpipes is a player of that instrument.

clue.text: Encouragement from easy run in training

indicators.note: in places the easy-run synonym inside the training abbreviation

parts.note: PT is physical training
a romp is an easy run or victory

explanation.surface: A coach gets motivation from a gentle jog during training.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt is a cue or nudge urging someone to act.

clue.text: Maintenance concerning partner

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in letters
to pair with someone is to partner them

explanation.surface: Upkeep matters to do with one's partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maintenance' hints at payments to an ex-partner but means upkeep.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping something in good condition means fixing it, which is upkeep or maintenance.

clue.text: Mad keeping close to commuter, it gives you bug

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the synonym for mad contains the other letters

parts.note: mad as in angry is irate

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An angry commuter complains of catching a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' looks like an infection but is the verb meaning annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to annoy them, a common informal synonym.

clue.text: Conjuring up job, auditor's division

parts.note: a calling is a vocation or job

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the next word is the one heard

parts.note: a fourth is one of four equal divisions

explanation.surface: An auditor's job is splitting accounts into divisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' suggests accounts but means a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon or evoke something, as a magician might, is to bring it out by magic: conjuring.

clue.text: Upcoming support artist embraced by warm patrons

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the whole is read from the bottom upwards
embraced by means held inside the synonym for warm

parts.note: snug means cosy and warm
aid is help or support
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A rising support act wins over a warmly enthusiastic audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upcoming' reverses the whole: AIDRA inside SNUG gives SNAIDRAUG, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrons are protectors or defenders of a cause, as guardians are.

clue.text: Chair of old chemical company found in lot

indicators.note: found in puts the company abbreviation inside the synonym for lot

parts.note: one's lot in life is one's fate
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a former British firm

explanation.surface: The chair of a defunct chemical firm turns up at an auction lot.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI (Imperial Chemical Industries) was a big British chemical company, taken over in 2008.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair a meeting is to preside over it, which is officiating.

clue.text: One fighting guilt is sadly under pressure

indicators.note: under places the anagram below the pressure letter in this down clue

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: sadly means things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fighter's guilt weighs on them under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer is someone whose sport is fighting with fists.

clue.text: Arm bits in Mississippi river

parts.note: in the US two bits is a quarter-dollar, so bits there are quarters
the Taff is a river in South Wales

explanation.surface: An arm with bits of it found in the Mississippi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm' is a weapon, not a limb; 'Mississippi' sets the American coin slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A long wooden pole used as a fighting weapon is an arm in the sense of a weapon.

clue.text: Veg succeeded for us, about time!

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
pro means in favour of, or for

indicators.note: about means round, so the word us goes around the time letter

explanation.surface: Someone finally gets vegetables served, and about time too.
explanation.definitionFit: Brussels sprouts are a classic green vegetable on the dinner plate.

clue.text: Furniture cut by man with large saw

indicators.note: cut by means split open by the other letters placed inside

parts.note: a bed is a piece of furniture
he refers to a man
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A man cuts up furniture with a large saw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like the tool but is the past tense of see.
explanation.definitionFit: Beheld is the past tense of behold, meaning looked at or saw.

clue.text: Measurement weight-watcher gathers in the morning

indicators.note: gathers means takes in, so the dieting word holds the morning letters

parts.note: a dieter watches their weight
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: A slimmer takes measurements every morning.
explanation.definitionFit: The width of a circle through its centre is a key measurement of length.

clue.text: Dummy and potty seldom deprived of son

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange
deprived of means the letter for son is removed

explanation.surface: A baby's dummy and potty are rarely without a son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potty' is the anagram signal, not the toilet; SELDOM without S gives ELDOM to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressmaker's dummy is a model figure, also a mannequin.

clue.text: Covers fish up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: a sprat is a small fish

explanation.surface: A fisherman covers up the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarpaulins, shortened informally, are waterproof sheets used as covers.

clue.text: Diminished? Not in the main

definitions.meaning: cut short, as with a reduced wage or a tail
a ship moored at a quay is out of the open sea, which is called the main

explanation.surface: Was something reduced? Not chiefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the old poetic name for the open sea, not 'mainly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay or tails are reduced when cut; a ship berthed at a quay is not out at sea.

clue.text: Beam signal to say stop doctor retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: a red light is the signal to stop
to doctor something is to rig or fiddle it

explanation.surface: A stop signal is beamed at a doctor who is retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: RED + RIG gives REDRIG, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A girder is a large metal beam supporting a building or bridge.

clue.text: Persistent university fellow returned to host club

indicators.note: to host is to hold inside, so the reversed word takes the club synonym in
returned means sent back, so the word for fellow is read backwards

parts.note: a dean is a senior fellow of a college
a bat is a club used in sport

explanation.surface: A university fellow comes back to entertain a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses DEAN to NAED, which then holds BAT: NA(BAT)ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that continues without lessening keeps going, i.e. persists.

clue.text: Tussle's broken out being pierced by variable needles

indicators.note: being pierced by puts the variable letter inside the anagram
broken out means a fight erupted, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A scuffle has erupted in which someone is stabbed with needles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken out' rearranges the letters of Tussle's to STLUSES, and the variable goes inside after the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Record-player needles are the pointed pieces that run in the groove.

clue.text: Regularly set reward by firm

indicators.note: regularly means at regular intervals, so every other letter of the run is taken

explanation.surface: A company pays a regular, fixed bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company but is the adjective meaning stable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something firm is stable, not shaking or wobbling.
